prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1267; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision in Conroe, Texas, where a westbound sedan and an eastbound sport utility vehicle came together head-on at low speed. Driver 1, the operator of the sedan, reported pain in the right shoulder and was evaluated at the scene. Driver 2, operator of the SUV, stated that the sequence of events matched what Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses gave accounts consistent with both drivers. Scene photographs were taken and show front-end damage to both vehicles that corresponds to the direction and force of the impact described by the parties. Responding officers confirmed that Passenger was seated in the sedan at the time of the collision and was not separately injured. Nothing observed at the scene suggested prior damage to either vehicle, and no earlier collision involving the sedan was reported to officers. Driver 1 was confirmed as a named insured on the policy covering the sedan. Officers issued no citations at the scene. This report is complete as of the time of filing and will be supplemented if additional information becomes available.
